planting.note: Direct sow around the last frost date; like the species, 'Alba' has a fragile taproot and resents transplanting, so sow it where it is to grow.

directions: Sow seed 1/2 inch deep directly in its permanent spot in any well-drained soil, including poor or dry ground, in full sun to light partial shade. 'Alba' is a true-breeding white-flowered strain of common borage, differing from the species only in flower color — pure white, star-shaped blooms replace the usual vivid blue — while retaining the same fuzzy gray-green leaves and mild cucumber flavor. The white flowers show up beautifully against the foliage and are prized by cooks for garnishing pale dishes, drinks, and desserts where a blue flower would clash. Deadhead spent flower stalks to extend bloom and limit volunteer seedlings, since it crosses readily with blue-flowered borage if both are grown nearby.
sources: Baker Creek Heirloom Seeds — white borage

subcategory: white-flowered culinary and medicinal hyssop cultivar

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6–8 weeks before last frost, surface-sown or barely covered, in full sun in lean, very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in zone 3–9; White Hyssop is a true-breeding white-flowered seed strain of common hyssop, matching the species in aromatic foliage and culinary/medicinal use.

directions: Sow White Hyssop indoors in a warm, well-drained starting mix; transplant after hardening off into lean, dry to moderately moist, alkaline-leaning soil in full sun. Prune back hard after the first flush of bloom to keep plants dense and bushy and to encourage a second round of flowers. The crisp white flower spikes make a striking contrast when planted alongside the standard blue-flowered species or the pink 'Roseus' strain in an herb or pollinator border, and the strongly camphor-scented leaves are harvested the same way as standard hyssop for bittering liqueurs, savory rubs, and traditional teas. Being a seed strain, some plants may show faint blush tones; rogue out off-color seedlings if pure white bloom is desired.
